questions.question: What is the difference between `my_list.append('item')` and `my_list.extend(['item'])`?
options: They do exactly the same thing
`append()` adds the string 'item', `extend()` adds each character separately
`append()` adds one item to the end, `extend()` adds each element from the list
`append()` creates a new list, `extend()` modifies the original
questions.explanation: `append()` adds its argument as a single item (even if it's a list), while `extend()` iterates through the iterable and adds each element individually. So `append(['A', 'B'])` adds one list, while `extend(['A', 'B'])` adds two separate items.

questions.question: Given `numbers = [10, 20, 30]`, what does `numbers.insert(1, 15)` do?
options: Replaces the item at index 1 with 15
Inserts 15 at index 1, shifting existing items to the right
Adds 15 to the end of the list
Causes an error because index 1 already exists
questions.explanation: `insert()` places the new item at the specified index and shifts all existing items to the right. So `numbers` becomes `[10, 15, 20, 30]`. The item that was at index `1` (`20`) moves to index `2`.

questions.question: Which statement about list mutability is TRUE?
options: Lists cannot be changed after creation
You can only add items to lists, not change existing ones
Lists are mutable, meaning they can be modified in place
Lists become immutable after the first modification
questions.explanation: Lists are mutable data structures, meaning you can change their contents after creation. You can modify existing items, add new items, remove items, and more—all without creating a new list.
